subsections.subsection_title: 46. HOW TO REPORT A NORMAL POSTNATAL EXAMINATION

blocks.text: **“This is a woman who is clinically well on the first postpartum day following an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is alert and comfortable, with stable observations. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are unremarkable. Her breasts are soft with no evidence of mastitis, and breastfeeding is progressing appropriately. The abdomen is soft and non-tender, and the uterus is firm, well contracted and appropriately involuted for the postpartum day. Lochia is within the expected range with no offensive odour or excessive bleeding. The perineum is healing appropriately with no evidence of haematoma** **or infection. There is no clinical evidence of DVT. I would also assess bladder and bowel function, psychological wellbeing, breastfeeding, contraception and VTE risk before discharge.”**
“The uterus is enlarged and boggy with poor tone, associated with excessive vaginal bleeding. This is concerning for primary PPH due to uterine atony and requires immediate management.”

“The patient is febrile and tachycardic with lower abdominal/uterine tenderness and offensive lochia. This is concerning for postpartum endometritis and requires urgent assessment and treatment for puerperal sepsis.”
“The Caesarean wound is erythematous, warm and tender with purulent discharge. These findings are consistent with a surgical site infection.”
“There is unilateral lower-limb swelling, warmth and tenderness. This is concerning for deep vein thrombosis and requires urgent investigation.”

“The patient has elevated blood pressure associated with severe headache and visual disturbance. I am concerned about postpartum pre-eclampsia and would arrange urgent senior assessment and management.”
